stimuli.text: Researchers collected data from 300 fifth-grade students. For each one, they recorded working memory span and reading comprehension score. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.52.

Researchers investigated whether the wording of a question changes what witnesses remember. They recruited 100 adult volunteers who watched a film of a car accident and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition were asked how fast the cars were going when they smashed into each other. Participants in the other condition were asked how fast the cars were going when they contacted each other. The researchers then recorded the speed in kilometers per hour that each participant wrote down.

Researchers investigated whether practice quizzes improve memory more than rereading. They recruited 120 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition read a passage once and then took three practice quizzes on it. Participants in the other condition read the same passage four times. The researchers then recorded the percentage of questions that each participant answered correctly on a test one week later.

Researchers collected data from 350 adults. For each one, they recorded the number of stressful life events in the past year and the number of colds in the past year. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.33.

Researchers investigated whether a smiling expression makes cartoons seem funnier. They recruited 90 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition held a pen between their teeth, which produces a smile. Participants in the other condition held a pen between their lips, which prevents a smile. The researchers then recorded the rating from 1 to 10 that each participant gave to a set of cartoons.

Researchers investigated whether the presence of other people slows the reporting of an emergency. They recruited 80 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition were filling in a form in a room with four other people when smoke began to enter the room. Participants in the other condition were filling in the form alone when smoke began to enter the room. The researchers then recorded the time in seconds before each participant left the room to report the smoke. The results are shown in the table. The difference between the two groups had a p value of 0.01.

rows.group: The group that waited with four other people

stimuli.text: Researchers collected data from 1,200 teenagers. For each one, they recorded the number of hours of social media use per day and score on a depression questionnaire. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.28.

Researchers investigated whether praise increases hand raising in class. They recruited 50 second-grade students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Children in one condition were praised by the teacher each time they raised a hand before speaking. Children in the other condition received no special response when they raised a hand. The researchers then recorded the number of times that each child raised a hand during one week.
Researchers collected data from 500 adults aged 20 to 80. For each one, they recorded age and score on a timed reasoning test. The correlation between the two measures was r = −0.55.
Researchers collected data from 250 adults. For each one, they recorded resting heart rate and self-rated anxiety. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.38.

Researchers collected data from 400 high school students. For each one, they recorded the average number of hours slept per night and grade point average. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.45.

Researchers investigated whether keeping a gratitude journal raises well-being. They recruited 110 adult volunteers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition wrote down three things they were grateful for every night for a month. Participants in the other condition wrote down three things they had done every night for a month. The researchers then recorded each participant's rating of life satisfaction on a scale from 1 to 10 at the end of the month.

Researchers investigated whether agreeing to a small request makes people more likely to agree to a large one. They recruited 120 homeowners and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Homeowners in one condition were first asked to sign a road-safety petition and two weeks later were asked to put a large sign in their garden. Homeowners in the other condition were only asked to put the large sign in their garden. The researchers then recorded the percentage of homeowners in each group who agreed to display the sign.
Researchers collected data from 450 adults. For each one, they recorded optimism score and the number of days of illness in a year. The correlation between the two measures was r = −0.30.

Researchers investigated whether guided hints help children learn to solve puzzles. They recruited 64 five-year-old children and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Children in one condition solved practice puzzles with hints from an adult that were gradually reduced. Children in the other condition solved the same practice puzzles alone. The researchers then recorded the number of new puzzles out of ten that each child later solved without help. The results are shown in the table. The difference between the two groups had a p value of 0.01.

Researchers investigated whether a new drug reduces anxiety. They recruited 150 adults diagnosed with generalized anxiety disorder and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition took the new drug every day for eight weeks. Participants in the other condition took a placebo pill that looked identical every day for eight weeks. The researchers then recorded each participant's score on a standard anxiety questionnaire after eight weeks.

Researchers collected data from 300 families. For each one, they recorded the warmth of parenting, as rated by observers and the child's self-esteem score. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.48.

Read the summary of a hypothetical study, then answer parts A to F.

**Introduction.** Researchers investigated whether guided hints help children learn to solve puzzles. They hypothesized that help from an adult would affect problem-solving skill.

**Participants.** The sample was 64 five-year-old children, recruited from one city. Parents gave informed consent, each child gave assent, and the plan was approved by an institutional review board. Families could withdraw at any time.

**Method.** The children were randomly assigned to one of two conditions. Children in one condition solved practice puzzles with hints from an adult that were gradually reduced. Children in the other condition solved the same practice puzzles alone. The researchers recorded the number of new puzzles out of ten that each child later solved without help.

**Results.** The group that received hints: mean new puzzles solved (out of 10) = 7.2. The group that practiced alone: mean new puzzles solved (out of 10) = 4.6. The difference was statistically significant (p = 0.01).

Use the three hypothetical sources to answer the question: **Does sleep improve memory?**

**Source A.** In an experiment, 60 students learned a list of word pairs at 9 p.m. Half were randomly assigned to sleep normally and half to stay awake all night. Twelve hours later, the sleep group recalled a mean of 31 pairs out of 40 and the awake group recalled a mean of 22 (p = 0.01).

**Source B.** Researchers recorded the brain activity of 25 adults in a sleep laboratory after they had learned a maze. The more slow-wave (NREM stage 3) sleep a participant had, the faster that participant completed the maze the next morning (r = +0.55).

**Source C.** A survey of 900 high school students found that those who reported sleeping fewer than six hours on school nights had lower average grades than those who slept eight hours or more. The researchers noted that students who slept less also reported more stress and more hours of paid work.

questions.stem: What does the correlation show?

options.text: The first measure causes the second
options.why: A correlation does not show cause and effect.

options.text: Higher values of the first measure tend to go with higher values of the second
options.why: Correct. A positive correlation means the two measures tend to move in the same direction.
A correlation of zero would show no relationship.

options.text: Higher values of the first measure tend to go with lower values of the second
options.why: That would be a negative correlation.

questions.explanation: A positive correlation means the two measures tend to move in the same direction.

questions.stem: A company gives applicants a test designed to predict how well they will learn computer programming. Which kind of test is this?

options.why: Correct. An aptitude test is a test that predicts a person's ability to learn or perform in the future.
An achievement test is a test that measures what a person has already learned.
A growth mindset is the belief that intelligence can be developed through effort and learning.
Stereotype lift is the boost in performance that comes from awareness that another group is negatively stereotyped.

questions.explanation: An aptitude test is a test that predicts a person's ability to learn or perform in the future.

questions.stem: As the evening gets darker, a gland in the brain releases a hormone that makes Priya drowsy. Which hormone is this?

options.why: Adrenaline is the hormone released by the adrenal glands that raises heart rate and energy during stress.
Correct. Melatonin is the hormone released by the pineal gland that makes a person sleepy.
Ghrelin is the hormone released by an empty stomach that increases hunger.
Oxytocin is the hormone that promotes bonding, trust and social attachment.

questions.explanation: Melatonin is the hormone released by the pineal gland that makes a person sleepy.

questions.stem: Inside the spinal cord, some cells link the incoming pain message to the outgoing movement message. Which cells are these?

options.why: Correct. Interneurons is the neurons inside the brain and spinal cord that pass messages between sensory inputs and motor outputs.
Glial cells is the cells that support, nourish, insulate and protect neurons.
The reflex arc is the simple automatic pathway in which the spinal cord produces a response before the brain is aware of the stimulus.
Sensory neurons is the neurons that carry incoming information from the sense receptors to the brain and spinal cord.

questions.explanation: Interneurons is the neurons inside the brain and spinal cord that pass messages between sensory inputs and motor outputs.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the operational definition of the dependent variable?

options.why: This is the independent variable.

options.text: The remembered speed of the cars
options.why: This names the variable but does not say how it was measured.

options.text: The random assignment of each one to a condition
options.why: This is a control procedure, not a definition of a variable.

options.text: The speed in kilometers per hour that each participant wrote down
options.why: Correct. An operational definition states exactly how a variable is measured.

questions.explanation: An operational definition states exactly how a variable is measured.

questions.stem: What is the dependent variable in this study?

options.text: The condition to which each one was assigned
options.why: This describes the independent variable.
This was manipulated by the researchers: it is the independent variable.
A hypothesis is a prediction, not a variable.
Correct. The dependent variable is the outcome that the researchers measured.

questions.explanation: The dependent variable is the outcome that the researchers measured.

questions.stem: After the birth of a new baby, a six-year-old starts sucking his thumb and talking like a toddler. Which defense mechanism is this?

options.why: Repression is the defense mechanism of pushing anxiety-arousing thoughts and memories out of awareness.
Correct. Regression is the defense mechanism of retreating to behavior from an earlier stage of development.
Sublimation is the defense mechanism of turning unacceptable impulses into socially valued activities.
Reaction formation is the defense mechanism of acting in the opposite way to one's unacceptable impulses.

questions.explanation: Regression is the defense mechanism of retreating to behavior from an earlier stage of development.

questions.stem: Positive psychologists group creativity, curiosity, judgment and love of learning under which virtue?

options.why: Courage is the category of character strengths that includes bravery, honesty and perseverance.
Temperance is the category of character strengths that includes forgiveness, humility and self-control.
Transcendence is the category of character strengths that includes gratitude, hope, humor and appreciation of beauty.
Correct. Wisdom is the category of character strengths that includes creativity, curiosity and love of learning.

questions.explanation: Wisdom is the category of character strengths that includes creativity, curiosity and love of learning.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the sensory and motor nerves that connect the brain and spinal cord to the rest of the body?

options.why: Correct. The peripheral nervous system is the sensory and motor nerves that connect the brain and spinal cord to the rest of the body.
The somatic nervous system is the division of the peripheral nervous system that controls voluntary movement of the skeletal muscles.
The autonomic nervous system is the division of the peripheral nervous system that controls glands and internal organs without conscious effort.
The sympathetic nervous system is the division of the autonomic nervous system that arouses the body for fight or flight.

questions.explanation: The peripheral nervous system is the sensory and motor nerves that connect the brain and spinal cord to the rest of the body.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes gross motor skills?

options.text: The laboratory apparatus with a glass-covered drop that is used to test depth perception in infants
options.why: That describes the visual cliff.

options.text: The movements that use small muscles, such as grasping a crayon or buttoning a shirt
options.why: That describes fine motor skills.

options.text: The movements that use large muscles, such as crawling, walking and jumping
options.why: Correct. This is what gross motor skills means.

options.text: The process by which some animals form a strong attachment to the first moving object they see
options.why: That describes imprinting.

questions.explanation: Gross motor skills is the movements that use large muscles, such as crawling, walking and jumping.

questions.stem: Hearing a song from her school days brings back a flood of memories for Tina. The song is acting as which of the following?

options.why: Recall is the retrieval of information without any cues, as in an essay question.
Correct. A retrieval cue is a stimulus that helps bring a memory to mind.
Recognition is the identification of previously learned information when it is presented, as in a multiple-choice question.
The testing effect is the finding that practicing retrieval improves memory more than rereading.

questions.explanation: A retrieval cue is a stimulus that helps bring a memory to mind.

questions.stem: A manager refuses to interview applicants who are over fifty, whatever their skills. This action is an example of which of the following?

options.why: A stereotype is a generalized belief about a group of people.
Prejudice is an unjustified negative attitude toward a group and its members.
The just-world phenomenon is the tendency to believe that people get what they deserve.
Correct. Discrimination is unjustified negative behavior toward a group and its members.

questions.explanation: Discrimination is unjustified negative behavior toward a group and its members.

questions.stem: Wearing masks in a large, excited crowd, normally law-abiding fans begin smashing windows. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Groupthink is the kind of thinking in which the desire for agreement in a group overrides a realistic evaluation of alternatives.
Correct. Deindividuation is the loss of self-awareness and self-restraint in group situations that provide arousal and anonymity.
Social facilitation is the improved performance on simple or well-learned tasks in the presence of others.
Social loafing is the tendency for people to put in less effort when working in a group than when working alone.

questions.explanation: Deindividuation is the loss of self-awareness and self-restraint in group situations that provide arousal and anonymity.

questions.stem: Researchers spend years examining one patient who lost his memory after surgery. Which research method is this?

options.why: Neuroplasticity is the brain's ability to change by reorganizing after damage or building new pathways through experience.
An fMRI is a scan that shows brain activity by tracking blood flow.
Lesioning is the destruction of a small area of brain tissue to study its function.
Correct. A case study is an in-depth study of one individual, such as a patient with unusual brain damage.

questions.explanation: A case study is an in-depth study of one individual, such as a patient with unusual brain damage.

questions.stem: Why is this study not an experiment?

options.text: The researchers did not manipulate a variable or randomly assign anyone to conditions
options.why: Correct. An experiment requires a manipulated independent variable and random assignment.
Experiments also test hypotheses.
Sample size does not determine the research method.
Experiments also use numerical data.

questions.explanation: An experiment requires a manipulated independent variable and random assignment.

questions.stem: What is the dependent variable in this study?

options.why: A hypothesis is a prediction, not a variable.

options.text: The facial expression produced by holding a pen
options.why: This was manipulated by the researchers: it is the independent variable.
Correct. The dependent variable is the outcome that the researchers measured.

options.text: The condition to which each one was assigned
options.why: This describes the independent variable.

questions.explanation: The dependent variable is the outcome that the researchers measured.

questions.stem: A child uses one mental category, 'chair', for stools, armchairs and benches. This mental category is an example of which of the following?

options.why: A schema is a mental framework that organizes and interprets information.
Assimilation is the interpretation of a new experience in terms of an existing schema.
Correct. A concept is a mental grouping of similar objects, events, ideas or people.
A prototype is the best or most typical example of a category.

questions.explanation: A concept is a mental grouping of similar objects, events, ideas or people.

questions.stem: After two years of long hours and constant pressure, a nurse feels drained, detached and ineffective. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: The social responsibility norm is the expectation that people will help those who need help, even at a cost to themselves.
Correct. Burnout is the physical and emotional exhaustion that results from long-term stress at work.
The social reciprocity norm is the expectation that people will help those who have helped them.
The bystander effect is the tendency for a person to be less likely to help when other people are present.

questions.explanation: Burnout is the physical and emotional exhaustion that results from long-term stress at work.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the strengthening of a behavior by removing an unpleasant stimulus after it?

options.why: Positive reinforcement is the strengthening of a behavior by adding a pleasant stimulus after it.
Correct. Negative reinforcement is the strengthening of a behavior by removing an unpleasant stimulus after it.
Positive punishment is the weakening of a behavior by adding an unpleasant stimulus after it.
Negative punishment is the weakening of a behavior by removing a pleasant stimulus after it.

questions.explanation: Negative reinforcement is the strengthening of a behavior by removing an unpleasant stimulus after it.

questions.stem: A harder pinch does not make an individual neuron fire a stronger impulse; each impulse has the same strength. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: The threshold is the level of stimulation that must be reached for a neuron to fire.
Depolarization is the change in which positive ions rush into the axon and make the inside less negative.
Correct. The all-or-nothing principle is the rule that a neuron either fires at full strength or does not fire at all.
The resting potential is the stable negative charge inside a neuron when it is not firing.

questions.explanation: The all-or-nothing principle is the rule that a neuron either fires at full strength or does not fire at all.

questions.stem: After flying across eight time zones, Kofi is wide awake at 3 a.m. and exhausted at noon. Jet lag is a disruption of which of the following?

options.why: Correct. The circadian rhythm is the body's roughly 24-hour cycle of wakefulness and sleep.
REM sleep is the sleep stage with rapid eye movements, vivid dreams, an active brain and relaxed muscles.
REM rebound is the tendency to have more REM sleep after being deprived of it.
NREM stage 1 is the brief, light first stage of sleep, in which a person may have hypnagogic sensations such as falling.

questions.explanation: The circadian rhythm is the body's roughly 24-hour cycle of wakefulness and sleep.

questions.stem: Which statement about the results is best supported?

options.text: The difference between the groups is statistically significant, so it is unlikely to be due to chance
options.why: Correct. A p value below 0.05 means a difference this large would rarely occur by chance alone.

options.text: The results prove that every individual in the first group differed from every individual in the second
options.why: The table reports group averages, not individual scores.

options.text: The difference between the groups is probably due to chance
options.why: A p value of 0.01 is below 0.05, so chance is an unlikely explanation.

options.text: The two groups had the same average result
options.why: The table shows different averages.

questions.explanation: A p value below 0.05 means a difference this large would rarely occur by chance alone.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the two-word stage in which a child uses mostly nouns and verbs, such as 'want juice'?

options.why: Correct. Telegraphic speech is the two-word stage in which a child uses mostly nouns and verbs, such as 'want juice'.
Cooing is the vowel-like sounds, such as 'ooh', that infants make from about two months.
Overgeneralization is the applying of a grammar rule too widely, as in 'goed' or 'mouses'.
Babbling is the stage from about four months in which infants produce many consonant-vowel sounds, such as 'ba-ba'.

questions.explanation: Telegraphic speech is the two-word stage in which a child uses mostly nouns and verbs, such as 'want juice'.

questions.stem: Tia loves parties, talks easily to strangers and feels energized by being with people. She would score high on which Big Five trait?

options.why: Conscientiousness is the Big Five trait of being organized, careful and self-disciplined.
Openness to experience is the Big Five trait of being imaginative, curious and willing to try new things.
Correct. Extraversion is the Big Five trait of being sociable, outgoing and energetic.
Emotional stability is the Big Five trait of being calm and secure rather than anxious and moody.

questions.explanation: Extraversion is the Big Five trait of being sociable, outgoing and energetic.

questions.stem: Which statement describes the directionality problem in this study?

options.text: It is unclear whether the correlation is positive or negative
options.why: The sign of r shows the direction of the relationship.

options.text: It is unclear whether the first measure influences the second or the second influences the first
options.why: Correct. A correlation cannot show which variable, if either, comes first.

options.text: It is unclear whether the two measures were recorded
options.why: Both measures were recorded.

options.text: It is unclear how many people took part
options.why: The sample size is stated.

questions.explanation: A correlation cannot show which variable, if either, comes first.

questions.stem: Walking to the phone, Rosa repeats a number again and again so that she does not forget it. Which technique is she using?

options.why: Elaborative rehearsal is the linking of new information to existing knowledge and meaning to store it in long-term memory.
Correct. Maintenance rehearsal is the repeating of information over and over to keep it in short-term memory.
Autobiographical memory is the memory of the events of one's own life.
Highly superior autobiographical memory is the rare ability to recall almost every day of one's life in detail.

questions.explanation: Maintenance rehearsal is the repeating of information over and over to keep it in short-term memory.

questions.stem: During surgery, a doctor stimulates a strip at the front of the parietal lobe and the patient reports feeling a touch on the cheek. Which area was stimulated?

options.why: The temporal lobes is the lobes above the ears, which process sound and help recognize language.
The motor cortex is the strip at the rear of the frontal lobes that controls voluntary movements.
Correct. The somatosensory cortex is the strip at the front of the parietal lobes that registers touch and body sensations.
The frontal lobes is the lobes behind the forehead, which handle planning, judgment and voluntary movement.

questions.explanation: The somatosensory cortex is the strip at the front of the parietal lobes that registers touch and body sensations.

questions.stem: A previously healthy student suddenly develops hallucinations after a period of intense stress and later recovers well. Which pattern of onset is this?

options.why: A positive symptom is a symptom of schizophrenia that adds an inappropriate behavior or experience, such as hallucinations.
The dopamine hypothesis is the idea that schizophrenia involves excessive activity of the neurotransmitter dopamine.
Correct. An acute onset is the sudden appearance of schizophrenia, often after stress, from which recovery is more likely.
A chronic course is the slow, gradual development of schizophrenia, from which recovery is less likely.

questions.explanation: An acute onset is the sudden appearance of schizophrenia, often after stress, from which recovery is more likely.

questions.stem: A therapist uses relaxation training with one client, examines thinking patterns with another and combines both with a third. Which approach is this?

options.why: The biopsychosocial model is the view that disorders result from the interaction of biological, psychological and social factors.
Correct. An eclectic approach is the use of techniques from several types of therapy, depending on the client's problem.
Comorbidity is the presence of two or more disorders in the same person at the same time.
The diathesis-stress model is the view that a disorder develops when an inherited vulnerability is triggered by stressful experience.

questions.explanation: An eclectic approach is the use of techniques from several types of therapy, depending on the client's problem.

questions.stem: Which of the following would be a confounding variable in this study?

options.text: The praised children were taught in a much smaller class
options.why: Correct. It differs between the groups along with the independent variable, so it could explain the results instead.

options.text: Each one was assigned to a condition at random
options.why: Random assignment reduces confounding; it is not a confound.

options.text: One group differed from the other in praise from the teacher
options.why: That is the independent variable itself.

options.text: The two groups differed in hand raising at the end of the study
options.why: That is the dependent variable, the result being measured.

questions.explanation: It differs between the groups along with the independent variable, so it could explain the results instead.

questions.stem: Seven students took a memory test. Their scores were 13, 6, 10, 8, 10, 18, 12. What is the mode of the scores?

options.why: Correct. The mode is the score that occurs most often.
That is the mean.
That is the range.
That is the highest score.

questions.explanation: In order, the scores are 6, 8, 10, 10, 12, 13, 18. The mode is the score that occurs most often. The one very high score pulls the mean (11) above the median (10), so the distribution is positively skewed.

questions.stem: Which research method did the researchers use?

options.why: A case study examines one individual in depth.
A meta-analysis combines the results of many studies.
Correct. The researchers measured two variables and examined their relationship without manipulating anything.
No variable was manipulated and there was no random assignment.

questions.explanation: The researchers measured two variables and examined their relationship without manipulating anything.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes a hallucinogen?

options.text: A drug, such as caffeine or cocaine, that speeds up neural activity and body functions
options.why: That describes a stimulant.

options.text: A drug, such as marijuana, that distorts perception and can cause sensory experiences without sensory input
options.why: Correct. This is what a hallucinogen means.

options.text: A drug, such as alcohol, that slows neural activity and body functions
options.why: That describes a depressant.

options.text: A drug, such as heroin, that relieves pain by acting on endorphin receptors and is highly addictive
options.why: That describes an opioid.

questions.explanation: A hallucinogen is a drug, such as marijuana, that distorts perception and can cause sensory experiences without sensory input.

questions.stem: Can the researchers conclude that resting heart rate causes a change in self-rated anxiety?

options.text: No, because correlations can only be calculated in experiments
options.why: Correlations are calculated in non-experimental studies.

options.text: Yes, because the sample was large
options.why: A large sample does not turn a correlation into evidence of causation.

options.text: No, because a correlation does not show cause and effect
options.why: Correct. Without manipulating a variable and assigning subjects at random, other explanations cannot be ruled out.

options.text: Yes, because the correlation is not zero
options.why: Any nonzero correlation still leaves the cause unknown.

questions.explanation: Without manipulating a variable and assigning subjects at random, other explanations cannot be ruled out.

questions.stem: If the data were shown on a scatterplot, what pattern would the points form?

options.text: A loose band that slopes downward from left to right
options.why: That would show a negative correlation.
Only a correlation of +1.00 or −1.00 gives a perfect line.

options.text: A loose band that slopes upward from left to right
options.why: Correct. A moderate positive correlation appears as a band of points sloping upward.

options.text: A shapeless cloud with no slope
options.why: That would show a correlation near zero.

questions.explanation: A moderate positive correlation appears as a band of points sloping upward.

questions.stem: Rats that wandered a maze with no reward for ten days ran it almost perfectly as soon as food was placed at the end. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Correct. Latent learning is learning that takes place without reinforcement and is not shown until there is a reason to show it.
Observational learning is learning by watching others and imitating them.
Modeling is the process of demonstrating a behavior that others then observe and imitate.
A cognitive map is a mental picture of the layout of one's surroundings.

questions.explanation: Latent learning is learning that takes place without reinforcement and is not shown until there is a reason to show it.

questions.stem: Which of the following would be a confounding variable in this study?

options.text: The gratitude group was also phoned each week by a friendly researcher
options.why: Correct. It differs between the groups along with the independent variable, so it could explain the results instead.

options.text: Each one was assigned to a condition at random
options.why: Random assignment reduces confounding; it is not a confound.

options.text: The two groups differed in subjective well-being at the end of the study
options.why: That is the dependent variable, the result being measured.

options.text: One group differed from the other in the type of journal
options.why: That is the independent variable itself.

questions.explanation: It differs between the groups along with the independent variable, so it could explain the results instead.

questions.stem: The night before a test, Gia studies for six hours without a break. Which kind of practice is she using?

options.why: The method of loci is the mnemonic of imagining items placed at locations along a familiar route.
Correct. Massed practice is study that is crammed into one long session.
A hierarchy is the organizing of information into broad categories divided into narrower ones.
Chunking is the organizing of items into familiar, manageable units.

questions.explanation: Massed practice is study that is crammed into one long session.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes thrill and adventure seeking?

options.text: The form of sensation seeking that involves a strong dislike of repetition and routine
options.why: That describes boredom susceptibility.

options.text: The form of sensation seeking that involves a desire for new experiences through travel, art and unusual lifestyles
options.why: That describes experience seeking.

options.text: The form of sensation seeking that involves a loss of self-restraint, as at wild parties
options.why: That describes disinhibition.

options.text: The form of sensation seeking that involves a desire for risky physical activities
options.why: Correct. This is what thrill and adventure seeking means.

questions.explanation: Thrill and adventure seeking is the form of sensation seeking that involves a desire for risky physical activities.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes closure?

options.text: The Gestalt principle that we fill in gaps to see a complete, whole object
options.why: Correct. This is what closure means.

options.text: The Gestalt principle that we group together objects that look alike
options.why: That describes similarity.

options.text: The Gestalt principle that we group together objects that are near each other
options.why: That describes proximity.

options.text: The Gestalt principle that we organize a scene into an object that stands out and its background
options.why: That describes figure and ground.

questions.explanation: Closure is the Gestalt principle that we fill in gaps to see a complete, whole object.

questions.stem: The group that first signed the petition agreed more often. The difference was statistically significant. Which conclusion is justified?

options.text: Whether a small request came first and compliance with a large request are related, but no cause can be inferred
options.why: That limit applies to correlational studies; this was an experiment.

options.text: The same result would be found in every group of people or animals
options.why: The sample limits how far the result can be generalized.

options.text: The hypothesis has been proved, so the study need not be repeated
options.why: Findings must be replicated; one study does not prove a hypothesis.

options.text: Whether a small request came first caused the difference in compliance with a large request
options.why: Correct. With random assignment and a manipulated variable, an experiment supports a conclusion about cause and effect.

questions.explanation: With random assignment and a manipulated variable, an experiment supports a conclusion about cause and effect.

questions.stem: Afraid of being trapped in a crowd or on a bus, Mr. Diaz has not left his house in six months. Which disorder does this suggest?

options.why: A specific phobia is the disorder in which a person has an intense, irrational fear of a particular object or situation.
Correct. Agoraphobia is the disorder in which a person fears and avoids public places from which escape might be difficult.
Social anxiety disorder is the disorder in which a person has an intense fear of being judged or embarrassed in social situations.
Ataque de nervios is the culture-bound anxiety syndrome, found mainly among people of Caribbean descent, marked by shouting, crying and a feeling of being out of control.

questions.explanation: Agoraphobia is the disorder in which a person fears and avoids public places from which escape might be difficult.

questions.stem: Which term refers to the first menstrual period?

options.why: Secondary sex characteristics is the nonreproductive traits of sexual maturity, such as body hair and a deeper voice.
Spermarche is a boy's first ejaculation.
Correct. Menarche is a girl's first menstrual period.
Menopause is the natural end of menstruation and of the ability to reproduce, usually around age 50.

questions.explanation: Menarche is a girl's first menstrual period.

questions.stem: A researcher who expects a drug to work smiles more at the patients who receive it and rates their improvement more generously. Which bias is this?

options.why: Correct. Experimenter bias is the influence of a researcher's expectations on the results of a study.
Self-report bias is the inaccuracy that arises when people describe their own behavior or feelings.
Social desirability bias is the tendency of participants to answer in a way that makes them look good.
Overconfidence is the tendency to be more certain than correct about one's own judgments.

questions.explanation: Experimenter bias is the influence of a researcher's expectations on the results of a study.

questions.stem: Which term describes an inflexible, long-standing pattern of behavior that begins by early adulthood and causes problems in relationships and work?

options.why: Correct. A personality disorder is a lasting, rigid pattern of behavior and inner experience that differs from cultural expectations and impairs functioning.
Cluster C is the group of personality disorders marked by anxious or fearful behavior: avoidant, dependent and obsessive-compulsive.
Cluster B is the group of personality disorders marked by dramatic, emotional or erratic behavior: antisocial, borderline, histrionic and narcissistic.
Cluster A is the group of personality disorders marked by odd or eccentric behavior: paranoid, schizoid and schizotypal.

questions.explanation: A personality disorder is a lasting, rigid pattern of behavior and inner experience that differs from cultural expectations and impairs functioning.

questions.stem: A nine-year-old takes pride in finishing his school projects well and compares his work with classmates' work. Which of Erikson's stages is this?

options.why: Correct. Industry versus inferiority is Erikson's stage in elementary school, in which children learn to feel competent or else feel inadequate.
Autonomy versus shame and doubt is Erikson's stage in toddlerhood, in which children learn to do things for themselves.
Initiative versus guilt is Erikson's stage in the preschool years, in which children learn to start tasks and carry out plans.
Trust versus mistrust is Erikson's stage in infancy, in which babies learn whether their needs will be met.

questions.explanation: Industry versus inferiority is Erikson's stage in elementary school, in which children learn to feel competent or else feel inadequate.

questions.stem: Which statement describes the directionality problem in this study?

options.text: It is unclear whether the two measures were recorded
options.why: Both measures were recorded.

options.text: It is unclear whether the correlation is positive or negative
options.why: The sign of r shows the direction of the relationship.

options.text: It is unclear whether the first measure influences the second or the second influences the first
options.why: Correct. A correlation cannot show which variable, if either, comes first.

options.text: It is unclear how many people took part
options.why: The sample size is stated.

questions.explanation: A correlation cannot show which variable, if either, comes first.

questions.stem: Years after losing his arm, a man still feels itching in the missing hand. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: The vestibular sense is the sense of balance and head position, based on the semicircular canals of the inner ear.
Kinesthesis is the sense of the position and movement of body parts, based on receptors in muscles and joints.
The gate control theory is the theory that the spinal cord has a gate that can block pain signals or let them pass to the brain.
Correct. Phantom limb sensation is the feeling of pain or touch in a limb that has been amputated.

questions.explanation: Phantom limb sensation is the feeling of pain or touch in a limb that has been amputated.

questions.stem: After an injury at the back of the brain, a gymnast can no longer keep her balance or make smooth movements. Which structure is most likely damaged?

options.why: Correct. The cerebellum is the structure at the back of the brainstem that coordinates balance, movement and procedural learning.
The thalamus is the brain's sensory relay station, which directs incoming signals to the cortex.
The pituitary gland is the master gland of the endocrine system, which is controlled by the hypothalamus.
The reticular activating system is the network of neurons in the brainstem that controls arousal and alertness.

questions.explanation: The cerebellum is the structure at the back of the brainstem that coordinates balance, movement and procedural learning.

questions.stem: Four studies of child development report these correlation coefficients: −0.86, −0.28, +0.20, +0.70. Which coefficient shows the weakest relationship?

options.why: +0.70 is farther from zero.
−0.86 is farther from zero.
Correct. Strength is the distance from zero, whatever the sign; +0.20 is closest to zero.
−0.28 is farther from zero.

questions.explanation: The sign of a correlation shows its direction; its distance from zero shows its strength. +0.20 is closest to zero.

questions.stem: A nine-year-old understands that pouring water into a taller glass does not change the amount, but she struggles with abstract algebra. Which of Piaget's stages is she in?

options.why: The preoperational stage is Piaget's stage from about age 2 to 7, in which children use words and images but cannot yet reason logically.
The formal operational stage is Piaget's stage from about age 12 on, in which people can reason about abstract and hypothetical ideas.
The sensorimotor stage is Piaget's stage from birth to about age 2, in which infants know the world through senses and actions.
Correct. The concrete operational stage is Piaget's stage from about age 7 to 11, in which children think logically about real objects and events.

questions.explanation: The concrete operational stage is Piaget's stage from about age 7 to 11, in which children think logically about real objects and events.

questions.stem: Mr. Diaz snores loudly, stops breathing many times each night, and feels exhausted during the day. Which sleep disorder does he most likely have?

options.why: Correct. Sleep apnea is a sleep disorder in which breathing repeatedly stops during sleep, causing brief awakenings.
REM sleep behavior disorder is a sleep disorder in which the normal paralysis of REM sleep is missing, so the person acts out dreams.
Insomnia is a sleep disorder with ongoing difficulty falling asleep or staying asleep.
Narcolepsy is a sleep disorder with sudden, uncontrollable attacks of sleep, often straight into REM sleep.

questions.explanation: Sleep apnea is a sleep disorder in which breathing repeatedly stops during sleep, causing brief awakenings.

questions.stem: Without ever being taught, salmon swim back to the stream where they hatched in order to breed. Which theory of motivation best explains this?

options.why: Incentive theory is the theory that behavior is pulled by rewards from outside the person.
The Yerkes-Dodson law is the principle that performance is best at a moderate level of arousal.
Correct. Instinct theory is the theory that behavior is driven by fixed, inborn patterns that are not learned.
Arousal theory is the theory that people are motivated to keep an ideal level of alertness and stimulation.

questions.explanation: Instinct theory is the theory that behavior is driven by fixed, inborn patterns that are not learned.

questions.stem: A patient with amnesia cannot remember practicing a puzzle, yet he solves it faster each day. Which kind of memory is still working?

options.why: Effortful processing is the encoding that requires attention and conscious effort.
Explicit memory is the memory of facts and experiences that a person can consciously recall and state.
Automatic processing is the encoding of information, such as space, time and frequency, without conscious effort.
Correct. Implicit memory is the memory of skills and learned associations that is retained without conscious recall.

questions.explanation: Implicit memory is the memory of skills and learned associations that is retained without conscious recall.

questions.stem: Researchers find that adults who suffered abuse and neglect as children have higher rates of illness and depression. These early events are called which of the following?

options.why: Emerging adulthood is the period from about 18 to the mid-twenties, between adolescence and full independence.
Correct. Adverse childhood experiences is the stressful or traumatic events in childhood, such as abuse or neglect, that raise the risk of later problems.
The imaginary audience is the belief of adolescents that everyone is watching and judging them.
Pretend play is the play in which children act out imaginary roles and situations.

questions.explanation: Adverse childhood experiences is the stressful or traumatic events in childhood, such as abuse or neglect, that raise the risk of later problems.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the direction of a person's enduring sexual attraction?

options.why: Correct. Sexual orientation is the direction of a person's enduring sexual attraction.
Gender is the socially and culturally influenced attitudes, feelings and behaviors that a culture links to being a boy, girl, man or woman.
A gender role is the set of behaviors that a culture expects of men or of women.
Gender identity is a person's own sense of being male, female, neither or some combination.

questions.explanation: Sexual orientation is the direction of a person's enduring sexual attraction.

questions.stem: Receptor cells in the eye change light energy into neural signals the brain can use. What is this process called?

options.why: Correct. Transduction is the conversion of physical energy, such as light or sound, into neural impulses.
The absolute threshold is the weakest level of a stimulus that a person can detect half of the time.
Sensory adaptation is the reduced sensitivity that follows constant, unchanging stimulation.
Weber's law is the principle that two stimuli must differ by a constant proportion, not a constant amount, to be noticed.

questions.explanation: Transduction is the conversion of physical energy, such as light or sound, into neural impulses.

questions.stem: Before a study begins, each adult volunteer reads a description of the procedures and risks and signs a form agreeing to take part. Which ethical requirement is this?

options.why: Deception is the misleading of participants about the true purpose of a study, allowed only when necessary and followed by debriefing.
Correct. Informed consent is the agreement of participants to take part after they have been told what a study involves.
Informed assent is the agreement of a minor to take part in a study, given in addition to a parent's consent.
An institutional review board is the committee that reviews research plans to make sure participants are treated ethically.

questions.explanation: Informed consent is the agreement of participants to take part after they have been told what a study involves.

questions.stem: Worried about a low grade that cannot be changed, Deb goes for a run and talks to a friend to feel calmer. Which kind of coping is this?

options.why: Problem-focused coping is the reducing of stress by changing the stressor itself or the way one deals with it.
Correct. Emotion-focused coping is the reducing of stress by managing one's emotional reaction rather than the stressor.
Immune suppression is the weakening of the body's defenses against illness during long-term stress.
Hypertension is persistently high blood pressure, which is made more likely by chronic stress.

questions.explanation: Emotion-focused coping is the reducing of stress by managing one's emotional reaction rather than the stressor.

questions.stem: Which statement about the results is best supported?

options.text: The two groups had the same average result
options.why: The table shows different averages.

options.text: The difference between the groups is statistically significant, so it is unlikely to be due to chance
options.why: Correct. A p value below 0.05 means a difference this large would rarely occur by chance alone.

options.text: The results prove that every individual in the first group differed from every individual in the second
options.why: The table reports group averages, not individual scores.

options.text: The difference between the groups is probably due to chance
options.why: A p value of 0.01 is below 0.05, so chance is an unlikely explanation.

questions.explanation: A p value below 0.05 means a difference this large would rarely occur by chance alone.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the activation, often without awareness, of certain associations that then influence perception or behavior?

options.why: The gambler's fallacy is the mistaken belief that a random event is more likely because it has not happened recently.
Correct. Priming is the activation, often without awareness, of certain associations that then influence perception or behavior.
The availability heuristic is the judging of how likely something is by how easily examples come to mind.
The sunk-cost fallacy is the tendency to keep investing in something because of what has already been spent on it.

questions.explanation: Priming is the activation, often without awareness, of certain associations that then influence perception or behavior.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the tendency to explain our own behavior by the situation but other people's behavior by their traits?

options.why: The self-serving bias is the tendency to credit our successes to ourselves and blame our failures on outside factors.
Correct. The actor-observer bias is the tendency to explain our own behavior by the situation but other people's behavior by their traits.
A pessimistic explanatory style is the habit of explaining bad events as lasting, affecting everything and caused by oneself.
Relative deprivation is the feeling of being worse off than the people one compares oneself with.

questions.explanation: The actor-observer bias is the tendency to explain our own behavior by the situation but other people's behavior by their traits.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as forgetting that happens because the information never entered long-term memory?

options.why: Retroactive interference is the disruption of older memories by new learning.
The forgetting curve is the pattern in which memory fades quickly at first and then levels off.
Correct. Encoding failure is forgetting that happens because the information never entered long-term memory.
The tip-of-the-tongue phenomenon is the temporary inability to retrieve a word that one is sure one knows.

questions.explanation: Encoding failure is forgetting that happens because the information never entered long-term memory.

questions.stem: In a drug trial, half of the patients receive the new medication. This half is which of the following?

options.why: Correct. The experimental group is the group in an experiment that receives the treatment being tested.
Statistical significance is the conclusion that a result is unlikely to have occurred by chance, usually when p is below 0.05.
Effect size is the measure of how large the difference or relationship found in a study is.
The placebo effect is an improvement that results from a person's expectation of a treatment rather than from the treatment itself.

questions.explanation: The experimental group is the group in an experiment that receives the treatment being tested.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes disorganized speech?

options.text: A lack of emotional expression in the face and voice
options.why: That describes flat affect.

options.text: A false belief, often of persecution or grandeur, that a person holds despite clear evidence against it
options.why: That describes a delusion.

options.text: The jumbled, illogical speech, sometimes called word salad, that is a symptom of schizophrenia
options.why: Correct. This is what disorganized speech means.

options.text: A sensory experience, such as hearing voices, that occurs without any outside stimulus
options.why: That describes a hallucination.

questions.explanation: Disorganized speech is the jumbled, illogical speech, sometimes called word salad, that is a symptom of schizophrenia.

questions.stem: A drug sits in the receptors for a neurotransmitter and prevents the neurotransmitter from having any effect. The drug is acting as which of the following?

options.why: Tolerance is the need for larger doses of a drug to get the same effect after repeated use.
Withdrawal is the unpleasant physical and psychological symptoms that follow stopping an addictive drug.
An agonist is a drug that increases the action of a neurotransmitter, for example by mimicking it.
Correct. An antagonist is a drug that decreases the action of a neurotransmitter, for example by blocking its receptors.

questions.explanation: An antagonist is a drug that decreases the action of a neurotransmitter, for example by blocking its receptors.

questions.stem: Because of her fears, Ana can no longer hold a job or see her friends. Which criterion for a psychological disorder does this meet?

options.why: Correct. Dysfunction is the criterion for a disorder that the behavior interferes with daily life, such as work and relationships.
Distress is the criterion for a disorder that the behavior causes suffering to the person.
The ICD is the World Health Organization's international system for classifying all diseases, including mental disorders.
Stigma is the negative attitudes and discrimination directed at people who have a psychological disorder.

questions.explanation: Dysfunction is the criterion for a disorder that the behavior interferes with daily life, such as work and relationships.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the disorder in which a person alternates between depression and a milder form of mania called hypomania?

options.why: Correct. Bipolar II disorder is the disorder in which a person alternates between depression and a milder form of mania called hypomania.
Mania is a state of extreme energy, overconfidence, racing thoughts and little need for sleep.
Major depressive disorder is the disorder in which a person has at least two weeks of depressed mood or loss of interest, with other symptoms such as changes in sleep and appetite.
Persistent depressive disorder is the disorder in which a person has a mildly depressed mood on most days for at least two years.

questions.explanation: Bipolar II disorder is the disorder in which a person alternates between depression and a milder form of mania called hypomania.

questions.stem: Scores on a university entrance test correlate strongly with students' later grades. Which quality does the test have?

options.why: Construct validity is the extent to which a test measures the concept it claims to measure.
Split-half reliability is the consistency of scores between two halves of the same test.
Test-retest reliability is the consistency of scores when the same people take the same test twice.
Correct. Predictive validity is the extent to which test scores forecast the future performance they are meant to predict.

questions.explanation: Predictive validity is the extent to which test scores forecast the future performance they are meant to predict.

questions.stem: Another research team repeats this study with new subjects and obtains the same result. What is this called?

options.why: Correct. Replication is repeating a study to see whether the finding holds.
That is an in-depth study of one individual.
That is how subjects are placed in conditions.
That is explaining the study to participants afterward.

questions.explanation: Replication is repeating a study to see whether the finding holds.

questions.stem: What does the correlation show?

options.text: Higher values of the first measure tend to go with higher values of the second
options.why: Correct. A positive correlation means the two measures tend to move in the same direction.
A correlation of zero would show no relationship.

options.text: Higher values of the first measure tend to go with lower values of the second
options.why: That would be a negative correlation.

options.text: The first measure causes the second
options.why: A correlation does not show cause and effect.

questions.explanation: A positive correlation means the two measures tend to move in the same direction.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the behavioral treatment that pairs an unwanted behavior with an unpleasant stimulus?

options.why: Applied behavior analysis is the use of the principles of conditioning to increase helpful behaviors and reduce harmful ones.
Correct. Aversion therapy is the behavioral treatment that pairs an unwanted behavior with an unpleasant stimulus.
A fear hierarchy is a list of feared situations arranged from the least to the most frightening.
Biofeedback is the technique of using electronic monitoring to show a person their body's signals so that they can learn to control them.

questions.explanation: Aversion therapy is the behavioral treatment that pairs an unwanted behavior with an unpleasant stimulus.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes rationalization?

options.text: The defense mechanism of refusing to accept a painful reality
options.why: That describes denial.

options.text: The defense mechanism of shifting an impulse from its real target to a safer one
options.why: That describes displacement.

options.text: The defense mechanism of giving a comfortable excuse in place of the real reason for a behavior
options.why: Correct. This is what rationalization means.

options.text: The defense mechanism of seeing one's own unacceptable impulses in other people
options.why: That describes projection.

questions.explanation: Rationalization is the defense mechanism of giving a comfortable excuse in place of the real reason for a behavior.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes shaping?

options.text: The passive giving up that follows repeated experiences of being unable to avoid bad events
options.why: That describes learned helplessness.

options.text: The reinforcing of closer and closer approximations of a desired behavior
options.why: Correct. This is what shaping means.

options.text: Thorndike's principle that behaviors followed by good outcomes become more likely and those followed by bad outcomes become less likely
options.why: That describes the law of effect.

options.text: A reinforcer, such as money or praise, that gets its power through association with other rewards
options.why: That describes a secondary reinforcer.

questions.explanation: Shaping is the reinforcing of closer and closer approximations of a desired behavior.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as a progressive brain disease that destroys memory and then other mental abilities?

options.why: Anterograde amnesia is the inability to form new memories after an injury or illness.
Retrograde amnesia is the loss of memories from before an injury or illness.
Infantile amnesia is the inability of adults to remember events from the first few years of life.
Correct. Alzheimer's disease is a progressive brain disease that destroys memory and then other mental abilities.

questions.explanation: Alzheimer's disease is a progressive brain disease that destroys memory and then other mental abilities.

questions.title: Article analysis: a study of problem-solving skill

parts.prompt: Identify the research method used in the study.

rubric.criterion: Identifies the method as an experiment.
rubric.example: The study is an experiment: the researchers manipulated a variable and randomly assigned the subjects to conditions.

parts.prompt: State the operational definition of problem-solving skill.

rubric.criterion: States how the variable was measured in this study.
rubric.example: Problem-solving skill was defined as the number of new puzzles out of ten that each child later solved without help.

parts.prompt: Describe the meaning of the difference between the two group averages.

rubric.criterion: Accurately describes which group scored higher or lower and what that means for the variable measured.
rubric.example: The group that received hints solved more new puzzles. On average, the value was 7.2 for the group that received hints and 4.6 for the group that practiced alone, and a p value of 0.01 means a difference this large is unlikely to be due to chance.

parts.prompt: Identify at least one ethical guideline applied by the researchers.

rubric.criterion: Identifies an ethical guideline that the summary shows was followed.
rubric.example: Informed consent and assent: parents consented and each child agreed to take part. (Also acceptable: approval by an institutional review board; the right to withdraw.)

parts.prompt: Explain the extent to which the research findings may or may not be generalizable, using specific and relevant evidence from the study.

rubric.criterion: Explains a limit (or strength) of generalizability with reference to the sample.
rubric.example: The sample was 64 five-year-old children from one city, so the findings may not apply to people of other ages, cultures or backgrounds. Because the sample was not randomly selected from a wider population, it may not be representative.

parts.prompt: Explain how at least one of the research findings supports or refutes the researchers' hypothesis.

rubric.criterion: Uses a specific finding from the study as evidence.
rubric.example: The group that received hints solved more new puzzles. (7.2 compared with 4.6).

rubric.criterion: Explains how the finding supports the hypothesis, using a psychological concept.
rubric.example: This supports the hypothesis that help from an adult affects problem-solving skill. Because subjects were randomly assigned, the difference can be attributed to help from an adult. The finding illustrates scaffolding within the zone of proximal development: temporary support lets a child master what they could not yet do alone.

questions.title: Evidence-based question: Does sleep improve memory?

parts.prompt: Propose a specific and defensible claim, based in psychological science, that responds to the question.

rubric.criterion: States a claim that answers the question and can be supported by the sources.
rubric.example: Sleep improves memory because memories are consolidated during sleep.

parts.prompt: (i) Support your claim using at least one piece of specific and relevant evidence from one of the sources. (ii) Explain how the evidence supports your claim, using a psychological perspective, theory, concept or research finding learned in AP Psychology.

rubric.criterion: Uses specific, relevant evidence from one source and names the source.
rubric.example: In Source A, students who slept recalled a mean of 31 of 40 word pairs, compared with 22 for students who stayed awake.

rubric.criterion: Explains how the evidence supports the claim.
rubric.example: This supports the claim through memory consolidation: during sleep, the hippocampus and cortex strengthen newly encoded memories, so the sleep group stored the word pairs better. Because the study was an experiment with random assignment, sleep can be said to have caused the difference.

rubric.criterion: Correctly applies a psychological concept in the explanation.
rubric.example: The concept must be named and applied correctly, as in the model explanation.

parts.prompt: (i) Support your claim using an additional piece of specific and relevant evidence from a different source. (ii) Explain how this evidence supports your claim, using a different psychological perspective, theory, concept or research finding.

rubric.criterion: Uses specific, relevant evidence from a different source and names the source.
rubric.example: In Source B, participants who had more slow-wave sleep completed the maze faster the next morning (r = +0.55).

rubric.criterion: Explains how the evidence supports the claim.
rubric.example: This supports the claim because NREM stage 3 sleep is linked to strengthening the neural connections formed during learning (long-term potentiation), so more deep sleep goes with better retention of the maze.

rubric.criterion: Correctly applies a different psychological concept from the one used in part B.
rubric.example: The concept must differ from the one used in part B and be applied correctly.
